subject: Post-incident technical readout: sequence drift, mitigation plan & validation steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@peakline.com>, Kara Morales <kara.morales@peakline.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident technical readout: sequence drift, mitigation plan & validation steps

Samir / Kara,

Thanks again for your patience overnight. Below is a concise readout of the event that impacted inference session continuity on Dec 4 (approx window: 02:14–02:46 UTC), the root cause we identified, actions we executed to contain the issue, and the proposed validation checks we will run with your team.

Executive summary:
- Event: a sequence-length distribution drift interacting with a recent eviction-time heuristic caused premature KV-cache eviction in a subset of Dedicated shards, which manifested as truncated or resumed sessions for long-context requests.
- Customer impact (Peakline): approximately 0.7% of token-generation sessions that relied on session-resume returned truncated completions during the window. Latency SLA remained within target for the majority of requests.

High-level timeline:
- 02:14 UTC: monitoring alerted to sustained long-context request rate increase for your pool; internal routing and autoscaling behaved as designed but exposed a kernel-selection corner case.
- 02:19 UTC: first customer reports of truncated outputs.
- 02:34 UTC: we rolled back the eviction heuristic configuration to the previous stable profile and blacklisted the affected shard pool from further canary rotations.
- 02:46 UTC: traffic and completion integrity returned to expected baselines.

Root cause (short):
A regression introduced in commit c4f9b2 adjusted the eviction-time calculation. Under sustained long-context loads the heuristic evaluated an edge-case distribution incorrectly, shortening the effective grace window for KV entries. That caused eviction of keys still needed for resumption in some sessions.

Immediate mitigations completed:
- Rollback to previous eviction heuristic (stable commit).
- Hotfix for kernel-selection path that incorrectly promoted a degraded execution branch.
- Blacklist of the affected Dedicated shard pool until validation passes.

What we will deliver to Peakline in the next 48 hours:
- An anonymized replay dataset of session traces for 02:00–03:00 UTC (attached: service-timeline.csv).
- RC A appendix that shows diff of the heuristic (attached: rca-appendix.pdf).
- Snippets from the kvcache logs around the eviction events (attached: kvcache-logs.txt).
- A validation plan: we will run 500 synthetic long-context sessions against your dedicated pool; expected pass-rate > 99.9%.

Proposed next step: 30-min sync tomorrow at 09:00 PT to walk through the artifacts and agree acceptance criteria. If that works, I will send a calendar invite.

If you need anything sooner, please ping me directly (dylan@redwood.com). We own end-to-end validation and will keep you updated at each milestone.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Lead, Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: service-timeline.csv (CSV stub); rca-appendix.pdf (summary + diffs); kvcache-logs.txt (snippet stubs)
From: Samir Gupta <samir@peakline.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Kara Morales <kara.morales@peakline.com>, Peakline Platform Team <platform@peakline.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-incident technical readout: sequence drift, mitigation plan & validation steps

Dylan —

Thanks for the concise write-up. A few quick clarifying questions before the sync: 

1) Can you confirm the exact impact window in UTC and the estimated number of affected sessions for Peakline production?
2) For the replay dataset, will you include the session identifiers (hashed/anonymized) so we can cross-check against our ingestion logs? We need that to validate acceptance criteria.
3) Is the rollback and kernel hotfix in the same change set or separate? We want to confirm there is no risk of a related regression in the hotfix path.

Also, our security/compliance team will likely request an excerpt of the audit trail for configuration changes during that window — can you flag who from Redwood will own that artifact?

If it's easier to cover these on the call, we can keep to the sync.

—Samir
Head of Platform Engineering
Peakline
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@peakline.com>, Kara Morales <kara.morales@peakline.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 14:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-incident technical readout: sequence drift, mitigation plan & validation steps

Samir — thanks for these calls-out. Short answers inline: 

> 1) Can you confirm the exact impact window in UTC and the estimated number of affected sessions for Peakline production?
- Confirmed impact window: 02:14:12–02:46:03 UTC (we will include per-shard counts in the replay CSV). Estimated affected sessions for your production pool: ~1,420 sessions (0.7% of the window traffic).

> 2) For the replay dataset, will you include the session identifiers (hashed/anonymized) so we can cross-check against our ingestion logs?
- Yes — session IDs will be salted and hashed; we will provide the salt mapping via a secure channel for reconciliation only.

> 3) Is the rollback and kernel hotfix in the same change set or separate?
- Separate: rollback is a revert of the heuristic (single revert commit). The kernel hotfix is a small independent patch to the selection guard. Both were applied and tested in isolation before the shard blacklist; neither touches customer-visible configuration beyond eviction timing behavior.

> Security/compliance audit trail owner?
- Karthik Iyer will own the audit artifact (configuration change logs + deploy traces). Karthik — can you confirm expected ETA for that package (timeline + who will sign off on the logs)?

Action items & owners (short):
- Replay dataset + anonymized session IDs — Dylan (DELIVER in 24h).
- Audit trail for config changes — Karthik (DELIVER in 48h).
- Validation runs and pass-rate report — Marcus / Evelyn (EXECUTE within 48h; report to Peakline and Dylan).

I will send the calendar invite for 09:00 PT tomorrow for the 30-min sync. Appreciate the quick feedback.

Best,
Dylan

Subject: Fwd: Post-incident technical readout: sequence drift, mitigation plan & validation steps

Team — forwarding Peakline's quick reply and our commitments. Short coordination notes below.

Context: Peakline asked for exact UTC window, hashed session IDs for reconciliation, and an audit trail for config changes. They want deliverables before tomorrow's sync.

Immediate asks (owners & due):
- Dylan: deliver anonymized replay CSV to Peakline and upload to the Drive link (service-timeline.csv) — due: 2026-12-06 15:00 PT.
- Karthik: compile and redact the config change audit trail (deploy IDs, who approved, timestamps, and rollback traces). Add a short write-up confirming rollout gating checks that were in place — due: 2026-12-07 09:00 PT.
- Marcus / Evelyn: schedule and run the validation harness (500 long-context sessions), collect pass/fail with raw logs; produce a one-page pass-rate summary — due: 2026-12-07 12:00 PT.

Notes: keep customer copies anonymized; share salt mapping only over the secure transfer (we'll use the signed SFTP link). Use the Drive folder below for artifacts: https://drive.redwood.com/Peakline/20261205/rca

Thanks — let's treat this as priority. I will update after the upload and after Karthik ack's the audit artifact.

Dylan
Account Lead, Reliability
Redwood Inference
